batch: OLP-0063–0068 First-order Logic proof-systems overview under the propositional profile
method: Fresh comparison of every exact frozen-English and Gujarati linguistic block, including the tokenized tableau title, with reverse paraphrases focused on inference direction, tree and sequence structure, assumption discharge, theorem and inconsistency conditions, semantic equivalences, historical qualifications and all four disclosed source repairs.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The chapter is Derivation Systems, under either the first-order or propositional profile selected by the frozen source tags.
samples.assessment: The conditional chapter identity, import scope and editorial placement guidance are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The editorial block says that this chapter collects general material about derivation systems and that a textbook using a particular system may place the introduction and relevant survey section before the chapter presenting that system.
samples.assessment: The conditional chapter identity, import scope and editorial placement guidance are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section is an introduction.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Logics generally have semantics and a derivation system; derivations provide a wholly syntactic, finite and mechanically checkable way to establish validity and consequence.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The earliest simple first-order systems are axiomatic: each formula in a sequence is an axiom or follows from earlier formulas by one of finitely many rules; these systems are mechanically checkable and metatheoretically manageable but difficult to construct and read.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Natural deduction, truth trees or tableaux, sequent calculus and resolution were developed for easier construction, understanding or mechanical use; most display derivations as trees so dependencies are visible.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Different calculi define theoremhood and derivability differently, but both the empty-premise and premise-relative provability relations should match semantic validity and consequence; the only-if directions are soundness.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The converse directions are completeness: a complete system derives every valid formula and every semantic consequence; first-order logic has such a system, first proved complete by Gödel in his 1929 dissertation.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A set is syntactically inconsistent when everything is derivable from it; consistency should coincide with satisfiability, with soundness and completeness supplying the two directions, and the two soundness forms and two completeness forms are respectively equivalent in classical first-order logic.
samples.assessment: The semantic and syntactic relations, both biconditional directions, historical qualifications and consistency equivalences are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section is the Sequent Calculus.
samples.assessment: Both sequent sides, rule directions, root conditions and empty-right inconsistency case agree after OLPRF-001.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A sequent is a pair of possibly empty sentence sequences separated by the sequent symbol, with independent lengths m and n; derivations are trees of sequents beginning with initial sequents and extended by rules that manipulate sides or introduce complex formulas. OLPRF-001 restores the right endpoint B_n.
samples.assessment: Both sequent sides, rule directions, root conditions and empty-right inconsistency case agree after OLPRF-001.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma proves A when a root sequent Gamma_0 ⇒ A has a derivation and every member of Gamma_0 belongs to Gamma; A is a theorem when ⇒ A has a derivation, illustrated by a two-step proof of (A∧B)→A.
samples.assessment: Both sequent sides, rule directions, root conditions and empty-right inconsistency case agree after OLPRF-001.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma is inconsistent when some left-only sequent Gamma_0 ⇒ has a derivation with all its members in Gamma; right weakening then derives any sentence.
samples.assessment: Both sequent sides, rule directions, root conditions and empty-right inconsistency case agree after OLPRF-001.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gentzen invented sequent calculus in the 1930s; its systematic symmetry makes it useful for theory and derivation search, although derivations can be hard to read, and many logics have such systems.
samples.assessment: Both sequent sides, rule directions, root conditions and empty-right inconsistency case agree after OLPRF-001.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section is Natural Deduction.
samples.assessment: Assumption scope, discharge labels, introduction and elimination directions, theorem condition and falsity rule are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Natural deduction formalizes patterns such as proof by cases, indirect proof and conditional proof; each connective and quantifier has introduction and elimination rules, with the stated implication, disjunction and conjunction examples.
samples.assessment: Assumption scope, discharge labels, introduction and elimination directions, theorem condition and falsity rule are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Natural-deduction derivations are formula trees whose leaves are assumptions; rules may discharge temporary assumptions, and the undischarged assumptions at the end jointly entail the conclusion.
samples.assessment: Assumption scope, discharge labels, introduction and elimination directions, theorem condition and falsity rule are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma proves A when a derivation ends in A and each undischarged leaf lies in Gamma; A is a theorem when every assumption is discharged, illustrated by a derivation of (A∧B)→A whose label 1 links discharge to implication introduction.
samples.assessment: Assumption scope, discharge labels, introduction and elimination directions, theorem condition and falsity rule are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma is inconsistent exactly when it derives falsity in natural deduction, and the falsity rule then permits derivation of every sentence.
samples.assessment: Assumption scope, discharge labels, introduction and elimination directions, theorem condition and falsity rule are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gentzen and Jaśkowski developed natural deduction in the 1930s, followed by Prawitz and Fitch; its natural proof patterns explain its philosophical and textbook use and motivate proof-theoretic semantics.
samples.assessment: Assumption scope, discharge labels, introduction and elimination directions, theorem condition and falsity rule are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The tokenized section title is Tableaux.
samples.assessment: Truth signs, branch geometry, closure quantifiers, rule labels, finite-premise scope and model extraction agree after OLPRF-002 through OLPRF-004.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Tableaux operate on signed formulas, each pairing T or F with a sentence, and arrange them in a downward-branching tree whose rules append formulas or split a branch.
samples.assessment: Truth signs, branch geometry, closure quantifiers, rule labels, finite-premise scope and model extraction agree after OLPRF-002 through OLPRF-004.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Rules decompose a complex signed formula into immediate signed subformulas and come in truth-sign pairs; the text gives the T∧ linear expansion, F∧ branching expansion and closure condition. OLPRF-002 restores the controlling F∧ rule name.
samples.assessment: Truth signs, branch geometry, closure quantifiers, rule labels, finite-premise scope and model extraction agree after OLPRF-002 through OLPRF-004.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma proves A when some finite Gamma_0⊆Gamma yields a closed tableau from F A and T-signed members of Gamma_0; the displayed closed tableau proves (A∧B)→A. OLPRF-004 restores the two true-conjunction rule labels in that tableau.
samples.assessment: Truth signs, branch geometry, closure quantifiers, rule labels, finite-premise scope and model extraction agree after OLPRF-002 through OLPRF-004.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma is tableau-inconsistent when a closed tableau has T B_1 through T B_n as assumptions and every B_i belongs to Gamma. OLPRF-003 restores this finite-subset scope.
samples.assessment: Truth signs, branch geometry, closure quantifiers, rule labels, finite-premise scope and model extraction agree after OLPRF-002 through OLPRF-004.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Beth and Hintikka independently invented tableaux in the 1950s and Smullyan simplified them; systematic construction supports automation, saturated open branches yield satisfying structures, and a closed tableau is essentially a compressed upside-down sequent derivation.
samples.assessment: Truth signs, branch geometry, closure quantifiers, rule labels, finite-premise scope and model extraction agree after OLPRF-002 through OLPRF-004.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section is Axiomatic Derivations.
samples.assessment: All three licensing alternatives, axiom schemas, modus-ponens dependencies, theorem condition and inconsistency consequence are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An axiomatic derivation is a sentence sequence in which every entry is an axiom, a member of Gamma or licensed by an inference rule; axiom schemas determine acceptable forms, the three displayed schemas govern implication, disjunction and conjunction, and very small primitive bases may use only one axiom.
samples.assessment: All three licensing alternatives, axiom schemas, modus-ponens dependencies, theorem condition and inconsistency consequence are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An inference rule gives a sufficient condition for licensing a sentence; modus ponens licenses B when earlier lines contain A and A→B.
samples.assessment: All three licensing alternatives, axiom schemas, modus-ponens dependencies, theorem condition and inconsistency consequence are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma proves A when a derivation ends in A and its assumption-licensed entries come from Gamma; A is a theorem when Gamma is empty. The three-line example is licensed by two axiom schemas followed by modus ponens.
samples.assessment: All three licensing alternatives, axiom schemas, modus-ponens dependencies, theorem condition and inconsistency consequence are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma is inconsistent when it derives falsity; a complete axiomatic system also proves falsity→A, so inconsistency yields every A.
samples.assessment: All three licensing alternatives, axiom schemas, modus-ponens dependencies, theorem condition and inconsistency consequence are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Frege introduced axiomatic logical systems in 1879, followed by Whitehead, Russell, Hilbert and his students; such systems are versatile and simple for metatheory but hard for finding and writing proofs.
samples.assessment: All three licensing alternatives, axiom schemas, modus-ponens dependencies, theorem condition and inconsistency consequence are preserved.
